name: Ollama
summary: One-command local runner for open-weight models, with a library of quantised builds and a simple API.
description:
Ollama made "run a model on my laptop" a single command. It ships a small model library of pre-quantised builds, pulls and caches them like container images, exposes a local HTTP API that most frameworks already know how to talk to, and handles the awkward parts — GPU detection, memory pressure, keeping a model warm — better than most people want to spend an afternoon on.

It is a runner, not a serving platform: throughput, batching and multi-user access are deliberately out of scope, which is why teams usually graduate to vLLM or a hosted provider the moment other people need the model too. Model quality is whatever the upstream weights are, and the convenience of one-command pulls makes it easy to forget that the licence on the model you pulled may not permit what your product does.
